about.title: Welcome to the official portal of Nazareth
about.description1: The heart of Christian faith. We understand that not everyone can physically visit Nazareth, a city where Jesus grew and where spiritual experiences await every visitor. Therefore, we are pleased to offer you the opportunity to bring Nazareth to you.
about.description2: Through our website, you can take a virtual tour of the main churches and holy sites of Nazareth, connect to the rich history and religious tradition that characterizes the place. In addition, we offer you a unique opportunity to purchase local souvenirs and even light a candle in memory or honor of your loved ones, as if you were here with us.
about.description3: In our online store, you can find a wide range of products: crosses made from local olive wood, jewelry inspired by Christian symbols, paintings, and mosaics that reflect the rich religious art, and more. Now, you can also buy water from the legendary Nazareth spring, sand from the sands of Nazareth, and local olives – all to feel the greatness of the city of Nazareth and Jesus. You can also choose to light a virtual candle, an act that conveys prayer and remembrance across distances.
about.description4: We invite you to open your hearts and feel the warmth of our community through every product you choose to buy. Every purchase supports the local community and helps preserve the rich heritage of Nazareth for future generations. Visit our website and find your way to connect with Nazareth, anytime and anywhere.

whatIsNew.touchingTheSacred: Touching the Sacred, Feeling the Heartbeat

introParagraphs.part1: Nazareth, the city where the miraculous unfolded, is the place where Jesus took His first steps, where the Virgin Mary embraced her Son and prayed for His safety. Here, within the ancient churches, at the sacred spring where Mary nourished Jesus, and in the vibrant market of the old city – you will find your faith coming to life once more.
introParagraphs.part2: Imagine yourself walking through the narrow streets, following in Jesus' footsteps to the churches, sharing moments of reflection at Mary's Spring, where the holy mother's eyes met the ancient waters. Every stone, every alley, tells a story of unwavering faith, of a spiritual journey that transcends time.
introParagraphs.part3: When you light a candle in the Basilica of the Annunciation, you reconnect with the place where Jesus first heard His divine calling. As your heart longs for Nazareth, our souvenirs carry the holy spirit of the city, reminding you of your deep connection to the place where it all began.
introParagraphs.part4: Allow us to bring Nazareth to you, straight into your home. With every memento, you preserve a deep bond with Nazareth – the city where Jesus and Mary walked, the city where faith was born. Remember the moments that happened here, the hearts that opened in prayer, and the tears that quietly fell upon the ancient stones.
introParagraphs.part5: Nazareth awaits you, embracing you from afar, bringing its holiness to you. Keep the flame burning in your heart, until the day you return to us – to the city where faith beats.

headerGreek.title: Explore the beauty of Greek Church

contentGreek.paragraph1: The Greek Orthodox Church of the Annunciation sits above the spring where Orthodox Christians believe the Annunciation took place. As the Virgin Mary went to draw water from the spring, the Archangel Gabriel appeared and informed her that she would conceive and give birth to a son who she would name Jesus. The current church dates back to 1750, when Daher al-Omar, the Bedouin ruler of the Galilee, gave the Greek Orthodox community permission to build it.
contentGreek.paragraph2: The church has a central nave with two aisles and contains a beautiful wooden iconostasis donated by a Greek merchant in 1767. The church was redecorated by Romanian artists from 1977 to 1978. An arched passageway leads down to a small chapel, which is decorated with Armenian tiles and has seven steps leading to the spring, believed to have been built by the Crusaders in the 12th century.
contentGreek.paragraph3: About 140 meters from the church is Mary’s Well, which was once fed by the spring and served as a local source of water for several centuries. The fountain was repaired in 1967 and again in 2000 but does not function today.

headerLatin.title: Explore the beauty of the Latin Church

contentLatin.paragraph1: The Latin Church, also known as the Basilica of the Annunciation, is a significant religious site located in Nazareth, Israel. It stands as one of the largest churches in the Middle East and holds deep religious significance for Christians worldwide.

history.title: Historical Background
history.text: The site is traditionally believed to be the place where the Angel Gabriel announced to the Virgin Mary that she would conceive and give birth to Jesus, an event known as the Annunciation. The basilica has a long history dating back to the early centuries of Christianity, with successive churches built on the site over time.

architecture.title: Architectural Features
architecture.text: The current basilica, constructed between 1955 and 1969, features a distinctive two-story structure. The upper church is used for worship services, while the lower church encloses the Grotto of the Annunciation, believed to be the actual site of the Annunciation. The basilica's architecture blends modern styles with traditional elements, and its interior is adorned with mosaics, frescoes, and artworks depicting scenes from the life of Christ.

visiting.title: Visiting the Basilica
visiting.text: The Basilica of the Annunciation is a popular destination for pilgrims and tourists visiting Nazareth. Visitors can explore both the upper and lower churches, admire the artistic and architectural features, and participate in religious ceremonies and events held at the basilica. The site offers a profound spiritual experience and serves as a symbol of faith and heritage.

headerMary.title: Explore the beauty of Mary's Well

contentMary.intro: Mary's Well, also known as the Well of the Virgin, is a significant historical and religious site located in Nazareth, Israel. It is traditionally believed to be the place where the Angel Gabriel announced to the Virgin Mary that she would bear Jesus, an event known as the Annunciation.

significance.title: Historical and Religious Significance
significance.biblicalText: According to Christian tradition, Mary's Well is where Mary was drawing water when the Angel Gabriel appeared to her and announced that she would conceive and give birth to Jesus Christ. This event is a central part of the Christian story of the Annunciation.
significance.culturalText: The well has been a vital source of water for the local community for centuries. It served as a gathering place for the people of Nazareth, making it an integral part of daily life in the town.
significance.architectureText: The well itself is part of a larger complex that includes the Greek Orthodox Church of the Annunciation. The current structure of the church dates back to the 18th century, but the well and the site have much older roots.

modern.title: Modern-Day Site
modern.restorationText: The fountain at Mary's Well has undergone several restorations over the years, notably in 1967 and 2000. Despite these efforts, the well does not function today as it once did.
modern.attractionText: Mary's Well is a popular destination for pilgrims and tourists. Visitors come to see the historic site and to experience the place where, according to tradition, the Annunciation took place.
modern.surroundingsText: The well is located in Nazareth's Old City, an area rich with historical and religious landmarks. Nearby attractions include the Basilica of the Annunciation, the Greek Orthodox Church of the Annunciation, and various other sites related to the life of Jesus and Mary.

visiting.title: Visiting Mary's Well
visiting.locationText: Mary's Well is situated in the heart of Nazareth, making it easily accessible for visitors exploring the Old City.
visiting.accessibilityText: The site is open to the public and can be visited throughout the year. It is advisable to check local visitor information for any specific visiting hours or guidelines.
visiting.culturalExperienceText: Visiting Mary's Well offers a unique opportunity to connect with the rich religious and cultural heritage of Nazareth. The site provides insight into the daily lives of the people in ancient times and their spiritual practices.

headerTitleNaz: Explore the beauty of Nazareth City

contentNaz.introduction: Nazareth’s Old City is most famous for its shuk (outdoor market) which attracts Israelis from across the country looking for traditional Arabic produce. This in itself is an experience, and a great contrast to the air-conditioned malls dotted around the country. For those interested in Christianity, the Old City and surrounds are filled with important Christian sites, including the Church of the Annunciation.

historicalSignificance.title: Historical and Religious Significance
historicalSignificance.text: Nazareth is prominently mentioned in the New Testament. According to Christian tradition, it is the site where the Angel Gabriel announced to Mary that she would bear Jesus, an event commemorated by the Basilica of the Annunciation. Archaeological evidence indicates that Nazareth was a small Jewish village during the time of Jesus. It has been continuously inhabited since antiquity.

modernNazareth.title: Modern Nazareth
modernNazareth.text: The city has a diverse population, predominantly Arab Muslims and Christians. As of recent estimates, Nazareth has around 77,000 residents. Nazareth is a vibrant cultural center with various religious, cultural, and educational institutions. It hosts festivals and events that reflect its rich heritage and diverse community. Tourism is a significant part of Nazareth's economy, driven by its religious sites and historical landmarks. Additionally, the city has a mix of small businesses, shops, and markets contributing to its local economy.

accessibility.title: Accessibility and Tourism
accessibility.text: Nazareth is well-connected by road, with frequent bus services from major cities like Tel Aviv, Haifa, and Jerusalem. The city offers various accommodation options, from hotels to guesthouses, catering to the needs of tourists and pilgrims.

meta.title: Visitor guide to Nazareth
meta.description: Everything to prepare your visit to Nazareth: how to get there from Haifa, Tel Aviv and Ben Gurion airport, dress code, best seasons, safety, money and the weather by month.

hero.title: Visit Nazareth
hero.lead: Practical answers for pilgrims and travellers: getting there, what to wear, when to come and what to expect.

getting.title: How to reach Nazareth
getting.lead: Nazareth sits in the hills of Lower Galilee in northern Israel, an easy trip from the coast.

haifa.title: From Haifa
haifa.text: The simplest route: about 40 minutes by car or taxi, or about an hour by bus.

telaviv.title: From Tel Aviv
telaviv.text: About two hours by car. Buses and trains run to the north; by public transport the usual way is to travel to Haifa or Afula and change to a bus for Nazareth.

airport.title: From Ben Gurion Airport
airport.text: About two hours by car or taxi. By public transport, take the train to Haifa or Tel Aviv and continue by bus; a pre-booked shuttle or a rental car is the easiest.

local.title: Once you are in Nazareth
local.text: The holy sites are all within about 15 minutes' walk of each other, so you can park once and explore on foot. Parking in the centre is limited, so arrive early or use a car park at the edge of the old town.

dress.title: Dress code
dress.text: Churches ask visitors to cover shoulders and knees, women and men alike. A light scarf or shawl in your bag solves it. Wear comfortable shoes: the old lanes are steep and uneven.

etiquette.title: Etiquette
etiquette.text: Speak softly in the churches and put your phone on silent. Remove hats inside. Photography is usually allowed, but not during services; ask before photographing people.

seasons.title: Best seasons
seasons.text: Spring (March to May) and autumn (late September to November) are mild and the most pleasant for walking. Summer is hot and dry; winter is cool and rainy. Easter, Christmas and the Feast of the Annunciation on 25 March are the busiest and most moving times.

safety.title: Safety
safety.text: Nazareth is generally welcoming and calm, but conditions in the region can change. Check your government's travel advice before you go, follow local news, and keep valuables close in crowds.

money.title: Money
money.text: The currency is the Israeli new shekel (ILS, ₪). Cards are widely accepted and there are ATMs in the centre; carry some cash for market stalls and small cafés. Polite bargaining is part of shopping in the market.

language.title: Language
language.text: People speak Arabic and Hebrew, and in the places pilgrims visit you will find English and often other languages too. A few words of Arabic are always warmly received.

climate.title: Weather by month
climate.lead: Typical conditions in Nazareth: warm, dry summers and cool, wet winters.
climate.caption: Average daily temperatures and rainfall by month
climate.note: Figures are rounded long-term averages, for guidance only. Weather varies from year to year; check the forecast before you travel.

free.q: Are the churches free to enter?
free.a: Entry to the main churches is generally free and donations are welcome. Each church sets its own hours and rules, so check before your visit.

dress.a: Modest clothing that covers shoulders and knees, and comfortable shoes for steep lanes. Bring a light layer in winter and sun protection in summer.

days.q: How many days do I need?
days.a: Most pilgrims see the main holy sites in one full day. Two or three days let you slow down for prayer, the Old City market and trips around Galilee.

safe.a: Nazareth is generally calm and welcoming, but conditions in the region can change. Check your government's travel advice and local news before and during your trip.

season.q: When is the best time to visit?
season.a: Spring and autumn are the most comfortable. Summer is hot and winter is rainy. Easter, Christmas and 25 March (the Annunciation) are the busiest and most moving times.

meta.title: Nazareth in the Gospels
meta.description: Read the Gospel passages about Nazareth, from the Annunciation to Jesus in the synagogue, each with a short reflection and the holy site that keeps its memory alive.

hero.title: Nazareth in the Gospels
hero.lead: Eight passages that name Nazareth, in the order of the story, each paired with the place you can still visit.

intro.title: From the Annunciation to “Come and see”
intro.text: Nazareth appears in the Gospels as the town of the Annunciation and of the hidden years of Jesus. Read a passage, pause over the reflection, then follow the link to the holy site.

gospel.note: Quotations are given for reflection and may differ slightly from the Bible translation you use. Passages: Luke 1, 2 and 4; Matthew 2; John 1.

luke126.quote: In the sixth month, the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a city of Galilee named Nazareth, to a virgin pledged to be married to a man named Joseph, of the house of David. The virgin’s name was Mary.
luke126.text: The whole story begins in a small hill town. Walk through Nazareth today and you walk where the Gospel begins.

luke130.text: Beneath the Basilica of the Annunciation lies the grotto that Christians have venerated for centuries as the place of Mary's home, where the angel's greeting is remembered.

luke138.text: Orthodox tradition remembers the angel first speaking to Mary as she went to draw water, at the spring beside the Greek Orthodox Church of the Annunciation. Her answer is the heart of every pilgrim's prayer.

matthew223.text: After the return from Egypt, Joseph settled his family in Nazareth. From then on Jesus was known as “Jesus of Nazareth”, and the name of the town travelled across the world.

luke240.text: Of the hidden years we are told very little: a child growing up in an ordinary town. The lanes and market of the Old City help you imagine that daily life.

luke251.quote: He went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them. His mother kept all these things in her heart.
luke251.text: For centuries the spring of Nazareth was where the town gathered each day. Standing at Mary's Well, you can picture the ordinary work and quiet faith that Mary kept in her heart.

luke416.quote: He came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up. On the Sabbath day he went into the synagogue, as was his custom, and stood up to read.
luke416.text: Jesus returned to preach in the town where he had grown up. Sites in the Old City, including a church traditionally placed on the site of the synagogue, recall that day.

john146.text: Philip's answer to Nathanael is the invitation of every pilgrimage: Come and see. Nazareth is still best understood by walking its streets.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.lead: Quick answers about visiting, praying with us and shopping. Cannot find yours? Write to us.

candle.q: How does lighting a candle work?
candle.a: Choose a church in Nazareth, write your prayer and pay {price}. We light a candle for you, record a short video with your name and send it to your e-mail address.

wall.a: Yes. A prayer appears on the wall with the name and country you enter. Do not include contact details, and use only your first name if you prefer.

live.q: Can I pray with you live?
live.a: Yes. Our live page broadcasts prayers and services from the holy sites of Nazareth and shows when the next broadcast starts.

pay.a: Payments are made with PayPal. Your card or PayPal details go to PayPal, never to us; we do not see or store them.

account.a: No. There are no accounts or passwords. Your cart and wishlist are kept in your own browser.

shipping.a: Shipping is a flat {shipping} per order, shown in your cart before you pay.

discount.a: Yes: {discount} off the items in every order, applied automatically in your cart.

damaged.q: What if my order arrives damaged?
damaged.a: Write to us with your order details and a photo. We will answer and put it right. See Shipping and returns for details.

donate.a: Yes. Donations from {min} to {max} are accepted through PayPal on the Donate page and support the work of Nazareth Holy Cross.

languages.q: Which languages is the site in?
languages.a: English, French, Spanish, German, Italian, Portuguese, Polish, Russian, Greek, Hebrew and Arabic.

data.a: Only what a service needs: orders, candle requests, prayers, reviews and contact messages. Read the Privacy policy for the details.

contact.a: Use the contact page or write to {email}.

meta.title: Privacy policy
meta.description: What personal data Nazareth Holy Cross keeps when you order, light a candle, share a prayer or write to us, why we keep it, and how to ask us to change or delete it.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.lead: We keep as little as we can. This page explains what we keep, why, and your choices.

who.title: Who we are
who.p1: This website is run by Nazareth Holy Cross, which shares the holy places, prayers and crafts of Nazareth with pilgrims everywhere. For any privacy question, write to {email}.

collect.title: What we collect
collect.p1: We collect only what you give us when you use a service:

items.orders: Orders: your name, e-mail address, phone number, delivery address, the items you bought, the total and the date.
items.candles: Candle requests: your name, e-mail address and your prayer.
items.prayers: The prayer wall: the name, country, category and prayer you write. These are shown publicly.
items.reviews: Reviews: your name, the place you are from and your message, shown on the site once approved.
items.contact: Contact messages: your name, e-mail address, phone number and message.
items.payments: Payments: handled by PayPal. We do not receive or store your card number.

items.u1: To fulfil and deliver your orders, and to light your candle and send you the video.
items.u3: To show prayers and approved reviews on the site, as you intended.

share.title: Who else sees it
share.p1: We do not sell your data. A few services help us run the site and process data on our behalf:

items.paypal: PayPal processes payments under its own privacy policy.
items.hosting: Our website, servers, database and image storage are run by hosting providers, which may store data outside your country.
items.maps: When you open a map or directions, or watch a video from another site, that site's own privacy policy applies.

browser.title: What stays in your browser
browser.p1: The site has no accounts and does not use advertising or analytics cookies. Your browser stores:

items.liked: The prayers you said Amen to, so that you can say it once.

keep.title: How long we keep it
keep.p1: We keep orders and candle requests for as long as we need them to serve you and to meet our legal and accounting duties. Prayers and reviews stay on the site until you ask us to remove them.

rights.title: Your choices
rights.p1: You can ask us to show, correct or delete the data we hold about you, or to remove your prayer or review. Write to {email} and we will respond. Depending on where you live, the law may give you further rights.

children.title: Children
children.p1: The site is not aimed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect their data. If you think a child has sent us data, write to us and we will delete it.

changes.title: Changes
changes.p1: If we change this policy we will update the date at the top of this page.

meta.title: Terms of use
meta.description: The terms for using the Nazareth Holy Cross website, ordering souvenirs, lighting candles, donating and sharing prayers and reviews.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.lead: Simple rules for using the site, ordering and sharing. By using the site you agree to them.

use.title: Using the site
use.p1: You may use this website for personal, non-commercial purposes. Please do not misuse it, try to break its security or send harmful or unlawful content.

orders.title: Orders and payment
orders.p1: Orders are paid through PayPal. Prices are in US dollars and are calculated by our server when you pay, not by your browser.

items.i1: Every order gets a discount of {discount} on the items and a flat shipping fee of {shipping}.
items.i2: We may cancel an order, with a full refund, if an item is unavailable or a price is clearly wrong.
items.i3: Delivery, customs and returns are explained in Shipping and returns.

candles.title: Candles
candles.p1: A prayer candle costs {price}. We light a candle for your intention in the church you choose and send you a video. It is a service of prayer and remembrance; we cannot promise a particular date or time.

donations.title: Donations
donations.p1: Donations are voluntary and support the work of Nazareth Holy Cross. If you donated by mistake, write to us as soon as possible.

content.title: Prayers and reviews
content.p1: When you share a prayer or a review, you tell us it is your own and that you are happy for it to be shown on the site.

items.i1: Do not post hateful, unlawful or misleading content, or other people's personal details.
items.i2: We may remove anything that breaks these rules or that we find inappropriate.

ip.title: Our content
ip.p1: The texts, photos, videos and design of the site belong to Nazareth Holy Cross or to the people who allowed us to use them. Please ask before you copy them for anything other than personal use.

info.title: Information on the site
info.p1: We do our best to keep the site correct, but opening hours, prices and travel conditions can change. Always check locally before you travel.

liability.title: Liability
liability.p1: The site and its services are provided as they are. To the extent the law allows, we are not responsible for losses caused by using the site or by events outside our control. Nothing here limits rights that the law gives you as a consumer.

changes.title: Changes
changes.p1: We may update these terms. The date at the top of the page shows the latest version.

meta.title: Shipping and returns
meta.description: Shipping costs, delivery, customs and what to do if an item arrives damaged: everything about receiving your Nazareth souvenirs.

shipping.title: Shipping and returns
shipping.lead: What you pay, when to expect your order and what to do if something is wrong.

cost.title: Cost
cost.p1: Shipping is a flat fee per order, however many items it contains.

items.i2: Discount: {discount} off the items, applied automatically. The total is shown in your cart before you pay.

delivery.title: Delivery
delivery.p1: We send souvenirs from Nazareth to addresses around the world. Delivery time depends on your country and the postal service. We will contact you by e-mail if we need anything from you.

customs.title: Customs and import duties
customs.p1: Orders sent abroad may be subject to import duties, taxes or customs fees set by your country. These are not included in our prices and are paid by the recipient.

returns.title: Damaged, wrong or missing items
returns.p1: If your order arrives damaged, is not what you ordered or is incomplete, we want to put it right.

items.i1: E-mail us with your name, the e-mail address used for the order and a photo of the problem.
items.i2: Keep the packaging until we have replied.
items.i3: We will tell you whether we send a replacement or refund you through PayPal.

digital.title: Candles and donations
digital.p1: Candle requests and donations are services, not products, so they are not shipped. If you made one by mistake, write to us.

contact.title: Questions
contact.p1: Write to {email} or use the contact page.
